content.title: Applied Machine Learning in Energy Data
content.intro: M1: Introduction to Sustainable Energy System Transformation

content.text:
This section is an introduction to the role of Machine Learning (ML) in energy policy, with a focus on structured data, supervised and unsupervised learning, and ethical considerations. It explains how ML models are trained using labeled data and test/train splits and how these models can support evidence-based policymaking in areas like energy access, consumption forecasting, and environmental impact.
The lesson moves from foundational ML concepts to specific applications, such as using Random Forests for solar energy 💬️ prediction and clustering for industrial emissions profiling. It concludes by exploring the limitations and ethical concerns tied to ML in public policy, including data bias, transparency, privacy, and explainability, and highlights best practices such as Privacy by Design, Explainable AI, and regulatory sandboxes.
